name: Beguiler
body:
The beguiler is a planner, a trickster and a magical infiltrator. They find ways to hide their magic, trick their marks and surprise their foes. They are a specialized spellcaster though some may not even know they cast spells. In any case, they know how to get what they want with the magic they have.

Role: The beguiler is a spellcaster that specializes in trickery and control. They do not have a lot of direct offensive capacity and are better served as supporting roleplaying, non-combat situations and aiding their more combat-oriented allies.

Alignment: Any. Beguilers can be of any alignment but those that err toward lawfulness are fewer than those that enjoy flaunting the rules.

Hit Die: d6

Starting Wealth: 2d6 x 10 (70 gp). In addition, each character begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

Class Skills

The beguiler’s class skills are: Acrobatics (Dex), Appraise (Int), Bluff (Cha), Climb (Str), Diplomacy (Cha), Disable Device (Dex), Disguise (Cha), Escape Artist (Dex), Knowledge (arcana) (Int), Knowledge (local) (Int), Knowledge (planes) (Int), Linguistics (Int), Perception (Wis), Perform (Cha), Profession (Wis), Sense Motive (Wis), Sleight of Hand (Dex), Spellcraft (Int), Stealth (Dex), Swim (Str), and Use Magic Device (Cha).

Skill Ranks per Level: 6 + Int modifier

Class Features

The following are the class features of the beguiler.

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

Beguilers are proficient with all simple weapons plus the hand crossbow, rapier, shortbow, short sword, and sword cane. Beguilers are also proficient with light armor, but not with shields. They can cast beguiler spells while wearing light armor without incurring the normal arcane spell failure chance. Like any other arcane spellcaster, a beguiler wearing medium armor, heavy armor, or a shield incurs a chance of arcane spell failure if the spell in question has a somatic component. A multi-class beguiler still incurs the normal arcane spell failure chance for arcane spells received from other classes.

Glib or Cunning

Every beguiler has some combination of glibness and cunning, however, they tend to focus on one or the other. The beguiler chooses either Intelligence or Charisma as their beguiler ability score.

Spellcasting

A beguiler casts arcane spells and must choose and prepare their spells ahead of time, like a wizard. The beguiler may learn, prepare, and cast any divination, enchantment, or illusion spell from the wizard or bard spell lists. If the spell appears on both lists, the beguiler can prepare the spell at the higher of the two levels. In addition to the spell schools, they may also learn, prepare, and cast the following spells:

Cantrips–arcane mark, dancing lights, mage hand, message, open/close, prestidigitation
1st-level-arcane pocket, cause fear, dancing lantern, expeditious retreat, feather fall, glue seal, grease, obscure poison, obscuring mist, peacebond, secluded grimoire, unseen servant, vocal alteration, wizened appearance, youthful appearance
2nd-level–alter self, false age, fog cloud, fool’s gold, glitterdust, knock, scare
3rd-level–blink, ghost light*, haste, impede speech, nondetection, secret page, slow, wall of mist
4th-level-adjustable polymorph, claim identity, control shadows*, enchantment foil, fear, solid fog
5th-level-greater blink*, greater glue seal*, greater grease, greater peacebond, passwall, sending, sudden etherealness*
6th-level-greater claim identity, mage’s decree
7th-level–instant summons
9th-level–etherealness

To learn, prepare, or cast a spell, the beguiler must have a beguiler ability score score equal to at least 10 + the spell level. The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against a beguiler’s spell is 10 + the spell level + their beguiler ability score modifier.

A beguiler can cast only a certain number of spells of each spell level per day. Their base daily spell allotment is given on the table below. In addition, they receive bonus spells per day if they have a high beguiler ability score (see Table: Ability Modifiers and Bonus Spells).

A beguiler may know any number of spells. They must choose and prepare their spells ahead of time by getting 8 hours of sleep and spending 1 hour studying their spellbook. While studying, the beguiler decides which spells to prepare.

Starting and New Spells: A beguiler begins play with a spellbook containing all 0-level spells from their spell list plus three 1st-level spells of their choice. The beguiler also selects a number of additional 1st-level spells equal to their beguiler ability score modifier to add to the spellbook. At each new beguiler level, they gain two new spells of any spell level or levels that they can cast (based on their new beguiler level) for their spellbook. At any time, a beguiler can also add spells found in other spellcaster’s spellbooks to their own, as long as the spell is on their spell list.

Cantrips: Beguilers can prepare a number of cantrips, or 0-level spells, each day, as noted on the table on page 2. These spells are cast like any other spell, but they are not expended when cast and may be used again.

Disguise Spell (Ex)

At 1st level, a beguiler can disguise what spell they are casting to throw off observers and other spellcasters attempting to counteract them. As a swift action when casting a beguiler spell, a beguiler can make a Bluff check opposed by an observer’s Spellcraft check. This can be activated when an observer rolls their Spellcraft check, it need not be activated prior. On a success, the beguiler can make it look like they are casting any other spell from the beguiler spell list or spell they know from advanced learning or another class they have of the same level. This can cause an observer to think they are simply casting a different more benign spell or attempt a counterspell with the wrong spell. Additionally, the beguiler gains a bonus on this Bluff check equal to 1/2 their class level.

Polyglot (Ex)

Beginning at 1st level, the beguiler becomes a master of languages to further enhance their trickery and subterfuge. They gain a new language and gain a bonus on Linguistics checks equal to 1/2 their class level. In addition, when casting a language-dependent spell against a creature for which they do not share a language, they can make a Linguistics check against a DC of 20 + the spell’s level to allow the target to be affected by the spell. This does not bypass other immunities like a mindless creature’s immunity to mind-affecting spells or if they have no language.

At 5th level, and every 4 levels thereafter, the beguiler gains another language.

Surprise Spell (Ex)

Starting at 1st level, a beguiler is adept at plying their spells against unwary foes. They gain a +1 bonus to the spell’s save DC when they cast a spell that targets any foe who would be denied a Dexterity bonus to AC (whether the target actually has a Dexterity bonus or not). This bonus to DC increases by 1 at 9th and 18th levels.

Trapfinding (Ex)

A beguiler adds 1/2 their class level to Perception skill checks made to locate traps and to Disable Device skill checks (minimum +1). A beguiler can use Disable Device to disarm magic traps.

Beguiling Talent: At 2nd level, and every 2 levels thereafter, the beguiler learns a talent to further expand their repertoire of tricks. They may select from the list starting later on this page. They must meet the listed prerequisites, if any, and no talent may be selected more than once, unless otherwise noted.

Spell Feint (Ex)

Beginning at 2nd level, the beguiler learns how to throw their enemy off and cast a spell.

When the beguiler successfully uses the Bluff skill to feint in combat, the target is denied their Dexterity bonus to AC and Reflex saves against the next beguiler spell they cast, in addition to the loss of AC against an attack. This does not allow them to gain the benefit to a spell and an attack in the same round on the same feint attempt. The beguiler must remain within melee distance of the target, unless a feat or ability allows for a feint at greater distance. Additionally, until the end of the beguiler’s next turn, the target cannot make attacks of opportunity against the beguiler for spells they cast. At 6th level, the beguiler can feint in combat as a move action. If they have, or later gain the Improved Feint feat, they may feint as a swift action. Additionally, any other feats that affect feints, may also be used for beguiler spells.

Advanced Learning (Ex)

At 3rd, 7th, 11th, 15th and 19th levels, the beguiler can add a new spell to their spell list, representing their own experimentation and techniques. The spell must come from the wizard spell list and be of a level of spell that the beguiler can cast.

The beguiler must still add the spell to their spellbook and prepare it as normal.

Silent Spell

At 5th level, the beguiler is treated as having the Silent Spell feat for metamagic purposes, though not for prerequisites, and it only applies to beguiler spells. If the beguiler already has or later gains the Silent Spell feat, applying the metamagic to beguiler spells does not increase the spell level of the spell. Additionally, they can apply the metamagic without preparing it ahead of time.

Still Spell

At 10th level, the beguiler is treated as having the Still Spell feat for metamagic purposes, though not for prerequisites, and it only applies to beguiler spells. If the beguiler already has, or later gains the Still Spell feat, applying the metamagic to beguiler spells does not increase the spell level of the spell. Additionally, they can apply the metamagic without preparing it ahead of time. They can’t rapidly apply or prepare without level increase using Silent and Still spell metamagic simultaneously.

Unstoppable Spell (Ex)

Beginning at 20th level, once per minute, if the beguiler successfully feints against a creature, the creature automatically fail their initial saving throw against the next spell. This only works with spells of the illusion or enchantment schools from the beguiler spell list.

Beguiling Talents
Arcane Artillerist (Su)

You gain 2 spells from the sorcerer/wizard spell list, these spells must be of a level you can cast. These spells must be from the evocation school and deal acid, cold, electricity, or fire damage. These spells are considered beguiler spells for ability purposes.

Arcane Potential (Su)

If you successfully feint a target, you can choose to forgo an attack or spell with the benefit of the feint to gain temporary hit points equal to your beguiler level plus your beguiler ability score modifier. The temporary hit points last for 1 minute and do not stack.

Armor of Geniality (Ex)

When you roll for initiative and until you damage a creature or take an action that would require another creature to make a saving throw, you gain a +2 bonus to AC and Will saving throws.

Bait and Switch (Ex)

If a target succeeds on a saving throw against one of your beguiler spells, you can quickly cast another spell upon the same target as a swift action. The second spell must have a casting time of a standard action or lower.

This second spell is treated as a spell feint if the original spell was also a spell feint. On your next turn, you are only able to use move actions.

Bypassing Spell (Su)

If you cast a spell against the target of your surprise spell ability, you can also reduce their spell resistance by 1/2 your class level (minimum 0).

Controlled Illusions (Su)

If you successfully disbelieve an illusion of a spell level you can cast, you can, as an immediate action, attempt to take control of the illusion spell by making a dispel check as dispel magic. If the dispel check is successful, you take control of the illusion spell as if you cast it.

Convincing Illusions (Su)

Prerequisite(s): 6th level or higher.

Anytime a creature attempts to disbelieve one of your illusion beguiler spells, you may make a caster level check and treat the DC of the spell as the higher of the spell’s original DC or the result of the caster level check.

Detailed Encoding (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): encoding beguiling talent.

You can attempt a DC 30 Bluff check to relay an incredibly detailed secret message including times, locations, and people. Additionally, you gain the Signature Skill feat for the Linguistics skill.

Dispelling Spell (Su)

Prerequisite(s): 8th level or higher

When casting a spell on a target that qualifies as a surprise spell, you may choose to forgo the bonus to the spell’s DC, and any other benefits granted by beguiling talents, to instead cast dispel magic on the target as a swift action, using your beguiler level as your class level.

Emboldening Spell (Su)

When casting a spell on a target that qualifies as a surprise spell, you may choose to forgo the bonus to the spell’s DC to instead grant yourself a circumstance bonus on saving throws equal to the bonus forgone for 1 round.

Enchanting Feedback (Su)

When targeted by an enchantment spell, if you succeed on your saving throw, you can send a painful mental feedback against the caster of the spell as an free action usable outside of your turn. The target takes damage equal to the spell level of the enchantment spell used plus your beguiler ability score modifier. This is a mind-affecting effect.

Encoding (Ex)

You are practiced at conveying secret messages and codes. You gain a bonus on Bluff checks to convey secret messages and to create forgeries equal to 1/2 their class level. Additionally, the amount by which you would need to fail your Bluff check to convey an incorrect message increases by the bonus.

Evasion (Ex)

If you make a successful Reflex saving throw against an attack that normally deals half damage on a successful save, you instead take no damage. Evasion can be used only if you are wearing light armor or no armor. If you are helpless, you do not gain the benefit of evasion.

Extinguishing Spell (Su)

When casting a spell on a target that qualifies as a surprise spell, you may choose to forgo the bonus to the spell’s DC, and other bonuses provided by beguiling talents, to instead extinguish all non-magical light sources carried or held by the target or within the spell’s area. You may instead attempt to dispel a magical light source as if using the dispel magic spell using your beguiler levels as your caster level. You may extinguish two light sources per bonus forgone.

False Spellcaster (Ex)

Whenever you successfully affect a foe with a spell that qualifies as a surprise spell, you may attempt a Bluff check as an immediate action (opposed by the target’s Sense Motive or Perception check, whichever has a higher bonus) before applying the effects of the spell to convince the target that another creature was the spellcaster. This Bluff check applies the normal modifiers for convincing a creature of a falsehood, but can be accomplished with just physical trickery (a shared language is not required). If the Bluff is successful, and you maintain concealment or cover, your stealth does not end.

Familiar (Ex)

You can acquire a familiar as the arcane bond wizard class feature, using your beguiler level as your wizard level to determine any of the statistics and abilities of the familiar. If you receive a familiar from another class, your levels of beguiler stack with the levels from that class when determining the familiar’s statistics and abilities.

Illusory Counterspell (Su)

You can ready an action to attempt to counterspell a spell targeting you or an ally within 30 feet. You must expend an illusion beguiler spell of a spell level at least one higher than the spell being cast. You instill the expended illusion spell into the spell being cast, turning it into an illusion. The target or targets of the spell may then make a Will save against DC 10 + the spell level that was mitigated by the illusion + the caster’s spellcasting ability modifier.

On a success the target disbelieves the spell, and is unaffected. The target gains a bonus on their Will save to disbelieve equal to 1/2 the spell level used to counter the affected spell.

Illusory Eyes (Su)

Prerequisite(s): 8th level or higher.

If you have an active figment or shadow spell of 3rd level or higher, You can focus your mind to see and hear through it as if you were in its area. As a move action you can switch your senses between the spell and yourself. While using the spell as the locus of your senses, you are blinded, deafened and lose any other senses around your physical body. You gain any extra-sensory effects, like divination spells or spell-enhanced senses when connected to the illusion spell. You must remain within 1 mile per beguiler class level of the figment or shadow spell. After 12th level this becomes 100 miles/class level. At 16th level, this becomes unlimited on the same plane and 20th it’s limitless.

Illusory Feint (Su)

If a creature fails a saving throw against a beguiler spell of the illusion school, they are considered to have been affected by a successful spell feint attempt by you.

Additionally, if an attacker misses you due to an illusory double, such as from the mirror image spell, you may make a spell feint attempt against them as an immediate action.

Improved Arcane Artillerist (Su)

Prerequisite(s): arcane artillerist beguiling talent, 8th level or higher.

You gain an additional 2 spells from the sorcerer/wizard list with the same restrictions as arcane artillerist. In addition, whenever you roll a ‘1’ on a damage die with an evocation spell you may treat that die as a ‘2’ instead.

Improved Bait and Switch (Su)

Prerequisite(s): bait and switch beguiling talent

This functions as the bait and switch beguiling talent except instead of casting a spell on the target of the original spell, you can cast a beneficial spell on yourself.

The restrictions and action costs are unchanged.

Improved Bypassing Spell (Su)

Prerequisite(s): bypassing spell beguiling talent

Any creature subject to your surprise spell ability from a beguiler spell is unable to apply any bonus to their saving throws against spells, like a dwarf’s natural resistance, or against mind affecting effects and their derivatives, like the bonus provided by a paladin’s aura.

Additionally, immunity to mind-affecting effects, or their derivatives like a paladin’s immunity to fear, is instead treated as a spell resistance of 30, and is thus reduced by the bypassing spell beguiling talent. This does not affect creatures immune to mind-affecting effects due to being mindless.

Improved Familiar (Su)

Prerequisite(s): You must have a familiar before selecting this beguiling talent.

You gain Improved Familiar as a bonus feat and may choose any familiar for which they meet the requirements.

Improved Infectious Charm (Su)

Prerequisite(s): infectious charms beguiling talent

This functions as infectious charms except that if a target affected by one of your charm or compulsion spells passes within 5 feet of another target, you can attempt to affect it as an immediate action, you may only do this once per original spell cast.

Infectious Charms (Su)

Prerequisite(s): 8th level or higher

When successfully affecting a target with a charm or compulsion spell, as a swift action you may affect another target within 30 feet. The secondary target may attempt the save against the spell as well and if they fail, the spell behaves in all ways as though it were the original target of the spell.

Inherent Decoding (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): encoding beguiling talent.

If exposed to a secret message whether verbal or written, you may automatically attempt a check to decode the message as long as you can see or hear it and the source is within 30 feet.

Knowledgeable Reflexes (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): 4th level or higher.

You can use your beguiler ability score modifier in place of your Dexterity for Reflex saves.

Liar (Su)

Prerequisite(s): 4th level or higher.

You gain spell resistance equal to 11 + your beguiler class level against any spell that detects, prevents, or reveals your lies.

This is applied even against spells or effects that would normally not allow for spell resistance, like discern lies.

The caster does not know they were thwarted by spell resistance.

Metamagic Feat

You can select a metamagic feat as a bonus feat instead of a beguiling talent.

Obscuring Spell (Su)

When casting a spell on a target that qualifies as a surprise spell, you may choose to forgo the bonus to the spell’s DC, and other benefits from beguiling talents, to have them treat all targets as if they had concealment for a number of rounds equal to 1/2 your beguiler class level. The miss-chance provided is equal to 15% per bonus forgone. A Fortitude save (DC 10 + 1/2 your beguiler level + your beguiler ability score modifier) reduces this effect to 1 round.

Opening the Third Eye (Su)

When you cast a divination beguiler spell, you open up a magical third eye on your forehead. You gain a +1 caster level on future divination spells, darkvision 60 ft., the benefits of detect magic and a bonus on Perception checks equal to the level of the divination spell cast.

This ability lasts for a number of rounds equal to the level of the spell cast. Multiple divination spells do not stack for this ability but do extend its duration to the greater of the new divination spell’s level or previous duration.

Opportune Spell (Su)

Prerequisite(s): Weapon Focus with a melee weapon or a class feature increasing attack rolls with a specific weapon or weapon group.

When you score a critical hit with a melee weapon attack you may cast an illusion or enchantment spell as a swift action as long as that spell has a casting time of no longer than one standard action.

Positioning Spell (Su)

When casting a spell on a target that qualifies as a surprise spell, you may choose to forgo the bonus to the spell’s DC, and other benefits from beguiling talents, to move up to 5 feet per DC bonus forgone. This movement does not provoke attacks of opportunity to those that are the target of the surprise spell.

Powerful Insight (Su)

After casting a divination spell, you can add your beguiler ability score modifier on combat maneuver checks and to your CMD for a number of rounds equal to the level of the divination spell cast.

Pressing the Advantage (Ex)

Prerequisite(s): 6th level or higher.

If you successfully affect a creature with a spell feint, as a full round action you can make an attack and cast a beguiler spell on the same target. The spell cast must have a casting time of standard action or less. The attack and spell can be made in either order, however whichever action is taken second takes either a -5 penalty to the attack roll or a -5 penalty to the spell save DC.

Redirect Attack (Su)

Prerequisite(s): 8th level or higher.

As an immediate action, you can expend a prepared spell slot to attempt to divert an attack. You make a caster level check and add twice the level of the spell level expended. If the result is higher than the attacker’s attack roll, the attack is diverted to another target of your choice within their reach or range. If there is no foe within the reach of the attacker, this ability fails but you do not expend the spell slot.

Redirect Spell (Su)

Prerequisite(s): 12th level or higher

As an immediate action, you can expend a prepared spell slot to attempt to divert a targeted spell. You make a caster level check and add twice the level of the spell level expended. If the result is greater than the spell DC or attack roll of the spell, the spell is directed to another target within their range. If there is no other possible target within range, the spell is an area of effect spell, or the spell allows neither save or attack roll, this ability fails but you do not expend the spell slot.

Shadowy Veil (Su)

If you cast an illusion beguiler spell with the shadow subschool, you gain a bonus to Stealth checks equal to the spell level cast and a concealment of 5% per spell level. This ability lasts for a number of rounds equal to the level of the spell cast.

Silencing Spell (Su)

When casting a spell on a target that qualifies as a surprise spell, you may choose to forgo the bonus to the spell’s DC, and other benefits from beguiling talents, to render them unable to speak or use verbal components for 1 round per bonus forgone. A Will save (DC 10 + 1/2 your beguiler level + your beguiler ability score modifier) negates this effect. This does not prevent the target from communicating via non-verbal or telepathic means.

Slowing Spell (Su)

When casting a spell on a target that qualifies as a surprise spell, you may choose to forgo the bonus to the spell’s DC, and other benefits from beguiling talents, to halve their movement speeds for 1 round per bonus forgone. A Fortitude save (DC 10 + 1/2 your beguiler level + your beguiler ability score modifier) negates this effect. If you affect a creature’s flight movement, its maneuverability is reduced by one step; if it’s airborne at the time, it falls unless it succeeds at a DC 10 Fly check.

Steal (Sp)

Prerequisite(s): 8th level or higher.

You can cast the spell telekinesis as a spell-like ability to call an object of 5 lbs. or less to your hand. This is usable at will, it has a caster level equal to your class level, and it uses your beguiler ability score modifier for its DC.

Steal the Light (Su)

When a creature fails a saving throw against a spell you cast which benefited from your surprise spell feature, that creature becomes dazzled and unable to make attacks of opportunity for one round. If the creature has light sensitivity they become dazed instead. This ability only applies to the initial saving throw of the spell.

Subvert Summoning (Su)

You can expend a spell slot against a target that you have successfully spell feinted as a standard action. If you do so, you can attempt to take control of a conjuration (summoning) spell for which the target has control. If you succeed on a caster level check against a DC of 11 + the spellcaster’s caster level, you take control of the summoning spell as if you were the original caster. The spell retains its original duration, though if it has a concentration component to the duration, you may take that on. You retain control of the creature for a number of rounds equal to the spell-level expended or the spell’s remaining duration, whichever is lower.

Unprepared Mind (Su)

If you successfully use spell feint against a target, they are also denied their Wisdom bonus to their Will saves, if any, against your next beguiler spell cast before the end of your next turn.

Weakness Highlighting Spell (Su)

When casting a spell on a target that qualifies as a surprise spell, you may choose to forgo the bonus to the spell’s DC, and other benefits from beguiling talents, to instead reduce the AC granted by armor or natural armor by double the bonus forgone until the beginning of your next turn.

Rogue Talents

You may choose one of the following rogue talents instead of a beguiling talent:

Canny observer, castling, charmer, coax information, convincing lie, disabling strike, fast fingers, fast picks, fast getaway, hairpin trick, hard to fool, heads up, honeyed words, last ditch effort, philologist, quick disable, quick disguise, scry slip, sleight of hand stunt, stealth stunt

Advanced Rogue Talents

Beginning at 10th level, you may choose one of the following advanced rogue talents instead of a beguiling talent:

Improved evasion (if you have evasion already), skill mastery, slippery mind, unwitting ally
